 From November 1, several key financial, tax and regulatory developments are set to come into focus, including changes to Goods and Services Tax (GST) rules, pensioners' life certificate submissions, and the extended income tax return filing deadline.
 This article highlights important November updates that every consumer, pensioner, and taxpayer should know.
 ADVERTISEMENT GST rule changes on post-sale discounts and refunds 
 In a notification dated October 26, the Government of India announced changes to GST provisions, including those governing post-sale discounts.
 What does this mean for businesses? 
 Earlier, businesses seeking to exclude post-sale discounts from the taxable value had to establish that the discounts were linked to an agreement entered into before the supply or were specifically linked to relevant invoices.
 From November 1, the revised provisions will ease these conditions. Eligible post-sale discounts can be excluded from the taxable value if the supplier issues a credit note and the recipient reverses the input tax credit attributable to the discount.
 Also Read: GST reforms to be rolled out in phases from November 1: CBIC member Sanjay Mangal In addition, provisional GST refunds for businesses facing inverted duty structures will be expedited. Under the revised mechanism, the automated system will quickly pay out GST refund claims without waiting for a manual officer.
 These measures, announced in the Union Budget for 2026-27, will come into effect from November 1.
 Pensioners' life certificate submission deadline ends on November 30 
 Generally, pensioners are required to submit an annual life certificate before November 30 every year.
 Pensioners below 80 years of age can submit their life certificates from November 1 to November 30. For pensioners aged 80 and above, the submission window opened on October 1.
 Beneficiaries who fail to submit the certificate within the prescribed period may face an interruption in their pension payments until the required document is furnished.
 Extended ITR filing deadline: Only for eligible taxpayers 
 The Income Tax Department had originally set October 31 as the deadline for filing income tax returns for the Assessment Year 2026-27 for the relevant category of taxpayers.
 However, considering taxpayers whose accounts are subject to audit, the department extended the return filing deadline to November 21, 2026.
 Note: This extension applies only to the specified categories of taxpayers and not to all individual taxpayers.
 Developments under watch 
 LPG cylinder prices
 At the beginning of every month, public sector oil marketing companies review LPG cylinder prices.
 As of October 30, the November 1 price revision had not been announced. Consumers are advised to check the latest rates announced by their LPG distributor before booking a refill.
 Revised disability pension guidelines
 The Union Cabinet has approved changes aimed at expanding disability pension coverage under the Pradhan Mantri Divyangjan Pension Yojana.
 As the revised operational guidelines are yet to be released, the reforms are not expected to come into force from November 1.
 Updates on bank services 
 Banks may continue to revise their fixed deposit and lending rates individually, depending on their respective policies and market conditions. Customers are advised to check the latest rates with their banks.
 Notably, several bank employee strikes and union protests are scheduled for November this year, over various service-related demands. Customers may check with the bank for updates on branch operations.
